Fitting and inference

Source: vignettes/articles/fitting-and-inference.Rmd
fitting-and-inference.Rmd

A small identifiable example

Unit-exponential residuals recover a Hawkes likelihood. With zero excitation, only the baseline is identifiable: the decay rate has no effect. Fix the excitation and decay parameters in this example.

model <- fspec(
  methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1),
  residual_law(c(rate = 1), stats::dexp, stats::pexp,
    stats::qexp, stats::rexp))
dt <- c(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5)
fit <- ffit(model, dt, optimizer = "stats", lambda_component0 = 0,
  fixed = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), control = list(reltol = 1e-12))
coef(fit)
#>    mu1 alpha1  beta1 
#>      3      0      1

There are three events in one unit of time; the baseline MLE is 3. The tighter optimizer tolerance makes this example easier to compare with that analytic answer; it does not validate inference for more complicated models.

Optimizers and parameter sharing

The default optimizer = "maxLik" requires the optional maxLik package. optimizer = "stats" uses R’s optim() or constrOptim() through emhawkes, without requiring maxLik. Controls differ: stats uses control$maxit, while maxLik uses control$iterlim.

By default, equal starting values within a numeric matrix share a parameter. Use reduced = FALSE for separate entries. Function parameters with the same name remain shared. Inspect coef(fit) to see the resulting names and order before specifying fixed parameters or constraints.

constraint and constraints are alternative spellings; supply one. Linear inequalities use list(ineqA = A, ineqB = B) for Aθ+B≥0A\theta + B \geq 0. Columns follow the full optimization parameter order, including fixed coordinates. The stats constrained optimizer requires an interior start and does not support equality constraints.

A valid = function(param) callback can reject invalid parameter proposals by returning FALSE. Its errors propagate; it should be deterministic.

Residual parameters and identification

Residual parameters are fixed by default. Set estimate_residual = TRUE to include them in estimation. This requires an identifiable model.

For example, with zero excitation and exponential residuals of rate rr, the event rate depends on the product rμr\mu. Estimating both freely cannot separate them. Fixing the residual rate or an appropriate kernel scale resolves that particular ambiguity. The package does not automatically normalize an arbitrary residual law or diagnose every form of nonidentification.

Inspect the result 

summary(fit)
#> FRPP maximum likelihood fit (stats, BFGS, bridge)
#> Log likelihood: 0.2958369
#> Convergence code: 0 (Normal convergence.)
#>        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> mu1      3.0000     1.7321  1.7321  0.08326 .
#> alpha1   0.0000     0.0000      NA       NA  
#> beta1    1.0000     0.0000      NA       NA  
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> Fixed parameters: alpha1, beta1
#> Wald covariance: available_unvalidated
fdiagnostics(fit)
#> $optimizer
#> [1] "stats"
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "BFGS"
#> 
#> $backend
#> [1] "bridge"
#> 
#> $optimizer_code
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $optimizer_message
#> [1] "Normal convergence."
#> 
#> $optimizer_success
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $estimate_residual
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $wald
#> [1] "available_unvalidated"
#> 
#> $reason
#> NULL
#> 
#> $active
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
#> 
#> $note
#> [1] "Optimizer curvature is not a validation of FRPP Wald coverage; no Hawkes Hessian stabilization is applied."
vcov(fit)
#>        mu1 alpha1 beta1
#> mu1      3      0     0
#> alpha1   0      0     0
#> beta1    0      0     0
c(AIC = AIC(fit), BIC = BIC(fit), events = nobs(fit))
#>       AIC       BIC    events 
#> 1.4083263 0.5069386 3.0000000

nobs() excludes the initial row. AIC and BIC describe the fitted likelihood; they do not establish that the model or its standard errors are appropriate.

fdiagnostics() reports convergence and Wald covariance availability. Covariance is withheld on optimizer failure, unavailable or nonpositive curvature, and detected constraint boundaries. A reported available_unvalidated covariance has not been checked for finite-sample confidence-interval coverage.

Weak identification, long-tailed estimates and nonsmooth residual densities can make Wald intervals unreliable. The moving transition in tzexp deserves particular care. Profile likelihood and bootstrap methods need separate validation; they are not implemented by ffit().

Restore and reuse a fitted model 

estimated <- fitted_fspec(fit)
initial <- finitial_state(fit)
replayed <- do.call(logLik, c(list(object = estimated, inter_arrival = dt), initial))
c(optimized = as.numeric(logLik(fit)), replayed = as.numeric(replayed))
#> optimized  replayed 
#> 0.2958369 0.2958369

fitted(fit) also returns the estimated model. finitial_state() describes the start of the fitted observation window, not the state after the final event. Continuing a path requires its terminal state.

Save results with saveRDS() and restore them with readRDS(). Captured callback environments remain references to external state; saving a fit does not automatically freeze that external state.
